why: M2-03 ruling CN11: which attribute carries a channel number, and in what
precedence order. The rule is stated twice, in two files two different
lanes own -- CHNO_ATTRS in bin/omarchy-iptv (the helper decides which
ATTRIBUTE) and CHNO_FIELDS in Model.js (the model decides what the value
MEANS). Nothing held the two statements together, so this file does:
tests/test_playlist.py and tests/Model.test.js both read it and drive
their own implementation against it (CLAUDE.md: a rule written twice gets
JSON rather than the .js of chno-cases: no QML engine reads this one, and
python cannot read a .js (ruling CN19 is about the parse vectors only).
notes: m3uAttributes is the helper's precedence order, highest first. The helper
lower-cases attribute keys before matching, so TVG-CHNO= is the same key.
cacheFields are the channels.json spellings the model reads BEFORE any
m3u attribute: `chno` is what the helper writes, the other two are what a
cache written by something else might carry. So the model's full order is
notRead is the other half of the contract: an attribute nobody agreed to
read must stay unread in BOTH implementations, or a playlist gains numbers
on one side of the cache and not the other.
maxMajor is the grammar's largest major (M2-03 1.2), stated in Model.js as
MAX_CHNO_MAJOR and in scripts/gen-playlist.py, which must never emit a
number the model will refuse: such a channel is displayed blank and cannot
be reached by digits, and a live pass would measure the wrong playlist with
